summary: Coos County, OR: two cabins and a 20-foot platform tower from the 1920s, an AWS post in 1942, and a 90-foot steel camera tower put up at the site in 2008, per one source.

facts.design: Two cabins and a 20-foot platform tower (1920s); a 16-by-16-foot shake cabin described in 1942
facts.status_note: Lookout removed and long abandoned; a 90-foot steel camera tower was erected at the former site in 2008 according to one source

events.note: Coos Bay Times, July 1927 (quoted by Forest Lookouts) describes the lookout as under construction; register says two cabins and a 20-foot platform tower in the 1920s
Jack Scott put in charge of the lookout (Coos Bay Times, July 1934)
Bert Palmer of Portland named lookout (Coos Bay Times, July 1941)
AWS post active March 18 to December 21, 1942; Roseburg Filter Center named
Register says AWS duties moved to a new lookout at McKeever's; a July 1942 letter describes Vaughn Peak being studied as the replacement
Coos FPA erected a 90-foot steel tower at the former lookout site as a base for a smoke-detection camera

corrections.why: The register describes a 20-foot platform tower (6.1 m); 27.4 m is 90 feet, the height of the steel camera tower Coos FPA erected at the site in 2008

notes_for_editor: Relocation is disputed: the register says a new lookout at McKeever's took over the AWS duties, while a July 1942 letter studied Vaughn Peak as the replacement. No source found confirms a McKeever's building. The 90-foot steel tower (2008) rests on one page and its current status is unknown; the record's 27.4 m height matches that tower, not the 1920s lookout. Access and current condition are not described by any source read. Web search for McKeever and a 2008 tower found nothing confirming these details. Confidence is low.
